lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: Levi's FY26 guide assumes incremental US tariffs of 20% on rest-of-world and 30% on China, and on the Q2 call the CFO said a ~$35m tariff benefit is not in guidance because he expected rates to go back to 19-20% in late July. Instead Section 122 (10%) was replaced on 24 July by Section 301 duties of 10% (Mexico, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Guatemala and others) or 12.5% (Vietnam and most others). The guide carries cost headroom that points to a raised FY gross margin/EPS outlook (~$0.07/share for the $35m alone) and a firmer Q4 implied guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises were bought: +10.65% (2026-04-07, Q1 beat and FY raise), +11.25% (2025-07-10). A raise whose midpoint sat below consensus was sold: -2.17% (2026-07-08, FY $1.46-1.52 against ~$1.51 FactSet, Q3 decel guide). A margin/tariff guide disappointment fell -12.55% (2025-10-09).

findings.finding: Levi paid ~$80m of IEEPA tariffs and at 31 May had recognised a refund asset only for CAPE phase 1 (10-Q note 9). The CFO said most of its refunds run through reconciliation entries, and CAPE Phase 2, which covers reconciliation-flagged entries, opened on 29 June, inside fiscal Q3 (1 June-30 August). A refund recognition of tens of millions in Q3 GAAP results is therefore likely, excluded from adjusted EPS as Gap's $417m was.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Levi refund print. Peers recognised refunds excluded from adjusted (Gap $417m in its August quarter). Across this repo's runs the tariff-refund names split by the direction of guidance, not by the refund.

findings.finding: Management called the Q3 step-down to +4-5% 'prudence' and 'conservatism' rather than demand deterioration, and said quarter-to-date trends supported the outlook. Levi beat EPS in Q1 (+$0.05) and Q2 (+$0.04, revenue +2.8% vs consensus). With consensus pinned at the top of the guide, a modest beat on revenue and EPS is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold on this name: 2025-10-09 a beat fell -12.55%, and 2026-07-08 a beat-and-raise closed -2.17% after opening ~-6% (shopappy). A plain beat is not what this stock pays for.

findings.finding: Peer and counterparty demand over Levi's exact quarter was flat to soft. H&M June-August sales were +1% in local currencies with September guided +1%. Kontoor's Wrangler US wholesale was flat. Gap's Old Navy comps were -4% (Gap brand +10%), Kohl's comps -0.9%, and American Eagle brand comps -1%. That gives little reason to expect Levi's wholesale to run well above its own cautious +4-5% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-08 reaction (-2.17%, opening ~-6%) was attributed to the Q3 growth deceleration and 'cautious consumer spending and uneven apparel demand'.

findings.finding: This is CFO Harmit Singh's last print. John Vandemore becomes CFO on 1 November 2026, per the 8-K of 30 September, which carried no guidance reaffirmation. The Q4 guide is set by an outgoing CFO who already called the H2 plan conservative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO transition print in the baseline window.

outside_window.finding: Section 301 rates of 10-12.5% against the 20% assumed (plus 0% on qualifying CAFTA-DR/USMCA apparel) are a full-year FY27 gross-margin tailwind, given inventory turns of ~2x. They show up fully only in the FY27 guide in January 2027, though tone may surface on this call.
CAPE Phase 3 (finally liquidated entries, CIT plaintiffs only) deploys 2026-10-06, after Levi's Q3 closed. Any further IEEPA refund recognition for Levi lands in Q4 FY26, reported in January 2027.

hunter_view.baseline_tension: Mixed: the negative findings run with the -9% five-day run-up but against the call bid (skew -2.27) and a 12.8% short. The refund and positioning findings agree with the skew, so the net lean is a small negative held close to 50.

findings.finding: The consensus revenue bar of $443.2m implies H1 FY27 sales growth of +5.2% ($402.1m + $443.2m against $371.7m + $431.8m), at the top of the CFO's 'low to mid single digits' H1 guide. Q1 also pulled $4-5m of Prime Day orders out of Q2. The guide's midpoint (about +4%) implies Q2 revenue near $433-434m, roughly 2% under the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock trades on the EPS guide, not sales: Q1 FY27 beat revenue by about 7% and raised the sales guide, and the stock still fell 10.2% on 2026-07-08 (baseline). The company beat its own Q1 expectations by a wide margin, so it has a record of guiding conservatively.

findings.finding: IEEPA refund upside. Helen of Troy said it had paid $71m of IEEPA tariffs outside Phase 1, and that its adjusted EPS and EBITDA outlook includes refunds, though only the ~$9.2m Phase 1. The Q1 10-Q says CBP launched Phase 2 on 2026-06-29 and the company was preparing claims, with receivables booked once 'probable of being recovered'. Any Phase 2 acceptance by the Q2 close on Aug 31 lands in adjusted EPS against a $0.50 bar that excludes it (about $0.03 per $1m pre-tax on ~23m shares). CBP's Phase 3 went live on 2026-10-06.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior refund print on this name. The Q1 Phase 1 recognition ($1.8m pre-tax) was in the quarter that fell 10.2% on a held EPS guide. Peer Hamilton Beach booked $36.5m of refunds into its Apr-Jun quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001709164/000170916426000157/hbbhc63026earningsreleasee.htm).

findings.finding: Management's stated policy is to reinvest 'the majority of over-performance back into the business' and 'the bulk' of refunds. Q1's beat therefore came with an unchanged adjusted EPS guide of $3.25-3.75, and the stock fell 10.2%. The same policy makes a held EPS guide the likely outcome again even if Q2 beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS guide moves drive this name: held guide after a beat -10.2% (2026-07-08), guide cuts -25.0% (2025-10-09) and -22.7% (2025-07-10), first FY27 guide +20.5% (2026-04-23), per the baseline.

findings.finding: The FY27 guide assumes 'tariff rates in place as of June 2026' (Section 122 at 10%). From 2026-07-24, USTR's Section 301 action set China/Hong Kong and Vietnam at 12.5%: a 2.5-point increase on the main sourcing countries for most of FY27's second half, not in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff-driven guide cuts drew -22.7% (2025-07-10) and -25.0% (2025-10-09) per the baseline. This increment is far smaller.

findings.finding: YETI's Apr-Jun quarter showed US drinkware flat 'amid category competition', with a 600bp drag on 2026 US drinkware growth from fading trend SKUs. That is a soft read-through for Hydro Flask, one brand inside the Home & Outdoor segment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Hydro Flask weakness was part of the FY26 sales declines that drew -22.7% and -25.0%. In Q1 FY27 Hydro Flask grew on distribution and Osprey was the strongest brand.

findings.finding: Positioning: 12.77% of float short with 9.0 days to cover (2026-09-15), into a -9.0% five-day slide on light volume with no identified cause, while the 25-delta skew is -2.27 (calls bid). Any guide that is not cut has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The one prior upside print (+20.5% on 2026-04-23, first FY27 guide) came with a large short base. Down prints have been large too, so shorts have not been punished every time.

outside_window.finding: CBP Phase 3 (entries liquidated more than 80 days ago, limited to importers with a CIT case pending) deployed 2026-10-06. Any cash from it for the rest of the $71m arrives over coming quarters, and the company has not said whether it has a CIT case. This is separate from any Q2 recognition, which is filed above.

Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): kept positioning as a finding under the core's filing rule but cut it from +1.0 to +0.7, carried by short interest and skew rather than the slide
